blocks.content:
Article 153 provides that there shall be a Governor for each State.

Key Points:
• Nominal executive head of the State
• Real executive power lies with the Chief Minister
• Appointed, not elected
• Acts as a link between Centre and State
Article 153 provides that there shall be a Governor for each State.

rows: Nominal executive head of the State

items: Remember that Article 153 establishes the provision for a Governor for each State.
Exams frequently contrast the Nominal Executive Head (Governor) with the Real Executive Power (Chief Minister).
Keep in mind that the Governor is appointed rather than elected to serve as a link between the Centre and State.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Article 153 mandates that there shall be a Governor for each State.
The Governor is the nominal executive head of the State.
Real executive power in a state lies with the Chief Minister.
The Governor is appointed, not elected.
The position acts as a crucial link between the Centre and the State.
